units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:

भीमभासदृढस्थित्या तवास्त्वतिविशोकता ||
units.iast:
dāmavyālakaṭanyāyo mā te bhavatu rāghava |
bhīmabhāsadṛḍhasthityā tavāstvativiśokatā ||
units.english: {0:The pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa} {1:may not} {3:become} {2:yours}, {4:descendant of Raghu}; {5:through the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha}, {6,7:let there be for you} {8:complete freedom from sorrow}.
units.sense: The pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa may not become yours, descendant of Raghu; through the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha, let there be for you complete freedom from sorrow.

grammar.karakaSummary: The two nominatives, nyāyaḥ and ativiśokatā, govern separate optative-prohibitive and imperative clauses; te/tava are possessive genitives, and sthityā is the instrumental means.
grammar.verbalModality: mā + loṭ bhavatu gives a prohibition; astu is loṭ 3sg expressing Vasiṣṭha's injunction/blessing.

words.gloss: the pattern illustrated by Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa
words.note: The Candrikā identifies Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa as the demons narrated below and nyāya as their unreflective mode of conduct.
With loṭ bhavatu, marks prohibition.
The surface enclitic te can also carry dative force; here it parallels tava and denotes possession.

words.gloss: let it become; may it be
words.note: mā supplies the prohibitive force.
Patronymic, not an opaque proper name in the translation.

words.gloss: through the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha
words.karaka: karaṇa, means by which ativiśokatā is to be

compound.vigraha: bhīmasya bhāsasya dṛḍhasya ca sthitiḥ; tayā

words.note: The Candrikā identifies the first three members as the names of another trio of demons.
Forms tavāstu by vowel sandhi: tava + astu.
The saṃhitā joins tava + astu as tavāstu.

compound.type: prādi formation: ati intensifies vi-śoka; vi- marks separation and is not nañ

words.note: ati intensifies the degree of vi-śoka, while vi- marks separation from sorrow; tal forms the abstract state: complete freedom from sorrow.

units.speaker: Rāma
units.english: {0:The pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa} and {1:the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha}—{2:O brahman}, {3,4:what has been said} {5:by you}, {6:remover of the affliction of becoming}?
units.sense: The pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa and the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha—O brahman, what has been said by you, remover of the affliction of becoming?

grammar.karakaSummary: kim is the interrogative content predicated by passive uktam; bhavatā is its instrumental agent, while brahman addresses Vasiṣṭha and apahāriṇā agrees with bhavatā.
grammar.verbalModality: uktam is a past passive participle used impersonally/neuter: 'what has been said?'

words.gloss: the pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa
words.note: Sandhi -aḥ + bh- gives the written -o.

words.gloss: the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha
words.note: The compound means the stance belonging to the named trio, not 'firm radiance.'

parts.gloss: brahman; here a masculine address to a sage

words.note: Masculine vocative address to Vasiṣṭha; the word itself does not say 'knower.'
Neuter agreement with uktam.

words.morph: past passive participle, nominative singular neuter
words.note: The root has the niṣṭhā formation ukta, not *vakta.

words.karaka: kartṛ expressed as instrumental agent of passive uktam
words.note: Respectful second-person reference.

words.gloss: by one whose nature is to remove the burning of becoming
words.morph: instrumental singular masculine agent noun, agreeing with bhavatā

compound.type: upapada-tatpuruṣa agent formation over ṣaṣṭhī relation

words.note: The Candrikā explicitly glosses bhavatāpāḥ as saṃsāra-duḥkhāni and apahārin as one habitually disposed to remove them.

words.gloss: the pattern of Dāma, Vyāla, and Kaṭa
words.note: Exact printed compound, with final anusvāra before m-.

words.gloss: the firm stance of Mīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha

words.note: Textually uncertain name: the edition and Muktābodha pair read mīma-, but 2.32 and both longer parallels read bhīma-. The source form is not normalized.

derivations.meaning: the firm stance of Bhīma, Bhāsa, and Dṛḍha
derivations.evidence: Laghu 2.32; Mokṣopāya/Yoga-Vāsiṣṭha parallels recorded in the source packet

words.karaka: prior action with same agent as kuru
words.note: The object is preceding tat.

words.karaka: finite verb in subordinate manner clause
words.note: The desiderative meaning is lexical to this Dhātupāṭha entry, not a san formation.

units.speaker: Vasiṣṭha
units.devanagari:

compound.vigraha: sarveṇa aiśvaryeṇa mano harati yat; tasmin

words.note: manohara preserves the image 'carrying away the mind,' hence delightful/captivating.

units.english: {0:Thus}, {2:when the hatred} {3:between the Dānavas and the gods} {1:had grown still firmer}, {4:the gods}, {6:having abandoned} {5:heaven}, {8:went} {9:out of sight} {7:in every direction}.
units.sense: Thus, when the hatred between the Dānavas and the gods had grown still firmer, the gods, having abandoned heaven, went out of sight in every direction.

grammar.karakaSummary: dṛḍhatarībhūte dveṣe forms a locative absolute, with dānava-devayoḥ a relational genitive dual. devāḥ is the agent of jagmuḥ; svargam the object of parityajya, dikṣu the locative spread, and adarśanam the resulting state/goal.
grammar.verbalModality: parityajya is a prior-action absolutive; jagmuḥ is perfect 3pl.

words.note: Connects the consequence to the preceding conflict.

words.affix: tarap comparative + cvi + kta + ṅi (saptamī ekavacana)
words.morph: past participle, locative singular masculine agreeing with dveṣe
words.note: The ī before bhū marks becoming what the comparative adjective denotes.
Source-backed action noun from √dviṣ, located in the background locative absolute.

units.english: {0:Then}, {2,3:whichever} {4:army-commanders} {5:are appointed} {1:by the Daitya Śambara} {6:with effort}, {11:the gods}, {10:intent on their endeavor}, {9:killed} {7,8:each and every one}.
units.sense: Then, whichever army-commanders are appointed by the Daitya Śambara with effort, the gods, intent on their endeavor, killed each and every one.

grammar.karakaSummary: The repeated ye ye introduces a distributive relative clause whose passive verb is kriyante and whose instrumental agent is Śambara-daityena; tāṃs tān is the matching distributive object of jaghnuḥ, with surāḥ agent and yatnaparāḥ qualifier.
grammar.verbalModality: kriyante is present passive 3pl; jaghnuḥ is perfect 3pl. The ya…ta correlation is explicitly distributive.

words.note: Advances the repeated sequence of appointments and defeats.

words.karaka: kartṛ expressed as instrumental agent of passive kriyante
words.note: Agent belongs only to the passive relative clause.

words.karaka: first member of distributive relative pair; theme of kriyante
words.note: Repeated with the next ye to mark distributive totality.

words.karaka: second member of distributive relative pair; theme of kriyante
words.note: The repetition ye ye means every corresponding set without exception.

units.english: {0:At last}, {3:Śambara}, {1,2:having fallen into agitation} and {4,5:exceedingly angry}, {6:created} {7:through māyā} {10:three} {8:terrible} {9:Asuras} {11:of great strength}.
units.sense: At last, Śambara, having fallen into agitation and exceedingly angry, created through māyā three terrible Asuras of great strength.

grammar.karakaSummary: Śambaraḥ is the agent of sasarja; udvegam is the complement of āpannaḥ, bhṛśam modifies kopavān, māyayā is instrumental means, and ghorān/asurān/trīn/mahābalān form the agreeing accusative object phrase.
grammar.verbalModality: āpannaḥ is a prior-result participle; sasarja is perfect 3sg. yāvat marks the narrative limit reached: 'until/at last.'
